extra_vocab.en: used to begin the story of how something started
extra_vocab.note: 說故事或解釋問題原因時的開場語，後面接一件起因事件。常見於同事閒聊、會議中說明狀況，語氣口語、自然。
extra_vocab.pattern: It all started when + S + V（過去式）
extra_vocab.grammar_note: when 後面要接完整子句（主詞＋動詞），且講過去的事用過去式；若後面只接名詞，要改用 It all started with + N。

examples.en: It all started when our main supplier raised its prices last spring.
examples.zh: 一切是從我們的主要供應商去年春天漲價開始的。

examples.en: It all started when a customer sent us a short complaint.
examples.zh: 一切是從一位顧客寄來一封簡短的抱怨信開始的。

examples.en: It all started when I missed the train to the airport.
examples.zh: 一切是從我錯過去機場的火車開始的。

examples.en: It all started when the team tried a new way to save time.
examples.zh: 一切是從團隊嘗試一種節省時間的新方法開始的。

similar.diff: 意思相同，但 少了 all，語氣較平淡、也比較適合書面。

example.en: It began when we changed the design of our website.
example.zh: 這一切是從我們更改網站設計開始的。

confusable.diff: with 後面接名詞，說明起因是什麼；when 後面接完整子句，說明起因事件。
confusable.usage: It all started with + 名詞；It all started when + 主詞＋動詞。

example.en: It all started with a simple question from a client.
example.zh: 一切是從一位客戶一個簡單的問題開始的。

extra_vocab.text: you will never guess what happened
extra_vocab.zh: 你絕對猜不到發生了什麼事
extra_vocab.en: used before you tell someone surprising news
extra_vocab.note: 口語開場語，用來吸引對方注意，接著講令人驚訝的事。多出現在同事閒聊或電話中，不適合正式書信。
extra_vocab.pattern: You will never guess + what／who／how much + S + V
extra_vocab.grammar_note: guess 後面接的是名詞子句，語序是 what + 主詞 + 動詞，不要寫成疑問句語序，例如不寫 what did happen。

examples.en: You will never guess what happened at the client meeting this morning.
examples.zh: 你絕對猜不到今天早上的客戶會議發生了什麼事。

examples.en: You will never guess who just signed the contract with us.
examples.zh: 你絕對猜不到剛跟我們簽約的人是誰。

examples.en: You will never guess what happened to my luggage at the airport.
examples.zh: 你絕對猜不到我的行李在機場發生了什麼事。

examples.en: You will never guess how much the supplier wanted for one box.
examples.zh: 你絕對猜不到供應商一箱要多少錢。

similar.diff: 更短、更口語，常單獨當開場；you will never guess 語氣更誇張，強調事情很出乎意料。

example.en: Guess what? We won the biggest order of the year.
example.zh: 你知道嗎？我們拿到了今年最大的訂單。

similar.diff: 說話者表達自己不敢相信；you will never guess 是在對聽的人賣關子。

example.en: I can't believe what happened to our shipment last week.
example.zh: 我不敢相信上星期我們的貨發生了那種事。

extra_vocab.zh: 事情一件接一件，最後演變成…
extra_vocab.en: one event caused the next, until something bigger happened
extra_vocab.note: 說故事時用來帶過中間的過程，直接帶到結果。常用來說明問題如何擴大，或事情如何發展到某個地步。
extra_vocab.pattern: One thing led to another, and + 結果
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 講過去發生的事用 led；講一般情況才用 one thing leads to another。後面常接 and 再說結果。

examples.en: One thing led to another, and we lost the contract.
examples.zh: 事情一件接一件，最後我們失去了合約。

examples.en: A small error appeared, one thing led to another, and the whole system stopped.
examples.zh: 出現一個小錯誤，接著事情一件接一件，最後整個系統停擺。

examples.en: We started with coffee, and one thing led to another: now we are partners.
examples.zh: 我們從喝咖啡開始，一步步發展下去，現在成了合夥人。

similar.diff: 強調時間很快過去；one thing led to another 強調事情一步步發展的過程。

example.en: We exchanged emails, and before long we became business partners.
example.zh: 我們互寄電子郵件，沒多久就成了生意夥伴。

similar.diff: 較正式，直接說明因果；one thing led to another 是整句固定說法，用來略過細節。

example.en: The mistake led to a long series of complaints.
example.zh: 這個錯誤引發了一連串的抱怨。

confusable.diff: one after another 是「一個接一個」，只表示連續，沒有因果；one thing led to another 有因果發展的意思。

example.en: Customers called one after another to complain about the delay.
example.zh: 顧客一個接一個打電話來抱怨延誤。

extra_vocab.note: 拼字檢查：正確拼法是 out of nowhere（nowhere 是一個字）。用來描述突然出現的人、事、消息，常見於會議、新聞與閒聊，語氣口語。
extra_vocab.pattern: N／事件 + came／appeared + out of nowhere
extra_vocab.grammar_note: nowhere 是一個字，不拆成 no where；out of nowhere 通常放在動詞或整句後面當副詞片語。

examples.en: A new competitor appeared out of nowhere and took half our customers.
examples.zh: 一個新的競爭對手突然冒出來，搶走我們一半的客戶。

examples.en: The client's order came out of nowhere, so we had no stock.
examples.zh: 客戶的訂單來得毫無預警，所以我們沒有庫存。

examples.en: A heavy storm came out of nowhere, and our flight was cancelled.
examples.zh: 一場大風暴突然襲來，我們的班機被取消了。

examples.en: The news of the merger came out of nowhere for most staff.
examples.zh: 對大多數員工來說，合併的消息來得毫無預警。

similar.diff: 強調時間上的「突然」，常放句首；out of nowhere 還帶有毫無預警、很意外的感覺。

example.en: All of a sudden, the screen went black during the presentation.
example.zh: 簡報進行到一半，螢幕突然變黑。

similar.diff: 較中性，強調事先沒有通知；out of nowhere 較口語、較戲劇化。

example.en: The server stopped working without warning on Monday morning.
example.zh: 伺服器星期一早上毫無預警地停止運作。

confusable.diff: 拼法相近，但 out of place 是「格格不入、不合適」，不是「突然」。

example.en: That red sofa looks out of place in our quiet office.
example.zh: 那張紅色沙發放在我們安靜的辦公室裡很不搭。

extra_vocab.zh: 等我回過神來、轉眼之間
extra_vocab.en: used to say something happened so fast that you did not notice it start
extra_vocab.note: 說故事時用來表示事情發生得很快、很突然，中間的過程自己沒有注意到。多用於閒聊或敘述經歷，語氣口語。
extra_vocab.pattern: The next thing I knew, + S + V（過去式）
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 後面接逗號與完整的過去式句子；主詞可依人物改成 she、he、we，如 the next thing she knew。

examples.en: I closed my eyes, and the next thing I knew, we had landed.
examples.zh: 我閉上眼睛，等我回過神來，飛機已經降落了。

examples.en: The next thing I knew, the manager was asking for my report.
examples.zh: 轉眼之間，經理就在跟我要報告了。

examples.en: I checked my bag, and the next thing I knew, my phone was gone.
examples.zh: 我檢查了一下包包，一轉眼手機就不見了。

examples.en: The next thing she knew, the deadline was only one day away.
examples.zh: 等她回過神來，截止日只剩一天了。

similar.diff: 強調時間過得很快；the next thing I knew 強調突然冒出一個新狀況。

example.en: Before I knew it, the meeting was over.
example.zh: 一轉眼，會議就結束了。

similar.diff: 單字副詞，較簡短、沒有「我沒注意到」的語感。

example.en: Suddenly, the lights went out in the whole office.
example.zh: 突然間，整間辦公室的燈都熄了。

extra_vocab.en: used to say that something was not what you expected
extra_vocab.note: 放在句首的插入語，說明事情的結果和自己預期的不一樣。商業英語常見，可用於會議紀錄、電子郵件與口語。
extra_vocab.grammar_note: surprise 用單數名詞，前面是 to + 所有格（my、our、his、her）：to my surprise，不寫 to surprise me。

examples.en: To my surprise, the client accepted our price without any discussion.
examples.zh: 令我驚訝的是，客戶沒有任何討論就接受了我們的價格。

examples.en: To our surprise, the new product sold out in two days.
examples.zh: 令我們驚訝的是，新產品兩天就賣完了。

examples.en: To his surprise, the hotel upgraded his room for free.
examples.zh: 令他驚訝的是，飯店免費幫他升等房間。

examples.en: To my surprise, sales rose even though we cut the advertising budget.
examples.zh: 令我驚訝的是，即使我們砍了廣告預算，銷售額還是上升。

similar.diff: 副詞，不指出是誰驚訝，語氣較客觀；to my surprise 是說話者個人的感受。

example.en: Surprisingly, the repair cost less than we had expected.
example.zh: 出乎意料的是，維修費比我們預期的還少。

similar.diff: 強調事情發生得出乎預料，不一定帶有個人感受。

example.en: Unexpectedly, the factory closed early on Friday.
example.zh: 出乎意料地，工廠星期五提早關閉。

confusable.diff: 意思接近，但寫法不同：I was surprised 後面接 that 子句。
confusable.usage: to my surprise 是放在句首的插入語，後面不加 that；be surprised 後面才可接 that 子句。

example.en: I was surprised that the meeting ended so early.
example.zh: 我很驚訝會議這麼早就結束了。

extra_vocab.en: used to say that something is true even if it is surprising
extra_vocab.note: 放在句首，先提醒對方：接下來要講的事雖然難以置信，但是真的。常見於閒聊、簡報開場與電子郵件中分享意外的事實。
extra_vocab.pattern: Believe it or not, + S + V
extra_vocab.grammar_note: 這是固定說法，it 不能換成其他字；通常放句首並加逗號，後面接完整句子。

examples.en: Believe it or not, our small team finished the project in two weeks.
examples.zh: 信不信由你，我們的小團隊兩週就完成了專案。

examples.en: Believe it or not, the old printer still works perfectly.
examples.zh: 信不信由你，那台舊印表機還是運作得很好。

examples.en: Believe it or not, the flight arrived thirty minutes early.
examples.zh: 信不信由你，班機提早了三十分鐘抵達。

examples.en: Believe it or not, most customers never read the user manual.
examples.zh: 信不信由你，大多數顧客從來不讀使用手冊。

similar.diff: 意思接近，語氣較正式、較書面；believe it or not 更口語。

example.en: Surprisingly enough, the cheapest supplier gave us the best service.
example.zh: 說來令人驚訝，最便宜的供應商給了我們最好的服務。

similar.diff: 後面常接 that 子句，直接說「很難相信」；believe it or not 是句首的插入語。

example.en: It is hard to believe that we sold ten thousand units in one day.
example.zh: 很難相信我們一天就賣出一萬件。

confusable.diff: 拼法節奏相似，但意思是「不論你喜不喜歡」，用來說明無法改變的事。

example.en: Like it or not, we must finish the report by Friday.
example.zh: 不管喜不喜歡，我們都必須在星期五前完成報告。

extra_vocab.en: used to say what you learned later, often something you did not expect
extra_vocab.note: 放在句首，引出事後才知道的真相，常和原本的想法形成對比。口語與書面都常見，語氣自然。
extra_vocab.pattern: As it turns out, + S + V
extra_vocab.grammar_note: as it turns out 後面接逗號與完整句；若要接 that 子句，可改成 It turned out that + S + V（過去事件用過去式）。

examples.en: As it turns out, the error was not in our report.
examples.zh: 結果發現，錯誤並不是出在我們的報告。

examples.en: As it turns out, the package had been sent to the wrong address.
examples.zh: 結果發現，包裹被寄到錯誤的地址了。

examples.en: As it turns out, the cheaper machine needed more repairs.
examples.zh: 結果發現，比較便宜的機器需要更多維修。

examples.en: As it turns out, the meeting was moved to next week.
examples.zh: 結果發現，會議被改到下星期了。

similar.diff: 意思相同，用過去式描述已發生的事，較像敘述；as it turns out 更口語，可放句首當插入語。

example.en: It turned out that the delay was caused by a software problem.
example.zh: 結果發現，延誤是軟體問題造成的。

similar.diff: 強調事實或對比，不一定是「後來才發現」。

example.en: In fact, the new design saved us ten percent.
example.zh: 事實上，新的設計幫我們省了百分之十。

confusable.diff: as it happens 是「碰巧」，說明剛好有某個巧合；as it turns out 是「結果才發現」。

example.en: As it happens, I have the file with me.
example.zh: 碰巧的是，我身上剛好帶著這份檔案。
